paper.title: Quantum Algorithms for Bandits with Knapsacks with Improved Regret and Time Complexities

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learner has quantum oracle access (quantum unitary oracles for reward and resource consumption), excluded by the ontology scope.
unmapped: Rewards and resource consumption accessed via quantum oracles (and their inverses) enabling quantum Monte Carlo estimation
d resources with resource consumption vectors in [0,1]^d; algorithm stops when any budget B is exhausted
settings.definition_quote: We consider the BwK problem with $m$ arms, $d$ resources, and a finite time horizon $T$. In each round $t\in[T]$, the algorithm selects an arm $i \in [m]$, receives a reward $r_t \in [0,1]$, and consumes a resource vector $\boldsymbol{c}_t \in [0,1]^d$. Each resource $j \in [d]$ is subject to a budget constraint $B_j\in\R^{+}$.

unmapped: Rewards and resource consumption accessed via quantum oracles enabling quantum Monte Carlo estimation
Assumption 1: LP relaxation has a unique, non-degenerate optimal solution (|I*| = |J*|)
The learner knows the problem-dependent quantities delta, chi, sigma and b=B/T used to set theta and epsilon in Algorithm 2
settings.definition_quote: We assume that for each arm $i\in[m]$, the reward and cost vectors are i.i.d.~drawn from an unknown distribution $\boldsymbol{\pi}_i$ supported on $[0,1]^{d+1}$. ... $\mathrm{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}}$ in \eq{primal-LP} has an unique optimal solution, and the optimal solution is non-degenerate: $\vert \mathcal{I}^* \vert = \vert \mathcal{J}^* \vert$.

symbols.OPT_LP: optimal value of the LP relaxation of the BwK problem

source.label: thm:main-independent
source.quote: The expected regret of \algo{quant-bwk1} satisfies $\mathrm{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}}-\mathrm{REW}\leq \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{\log (dT)}\right)\left(\mathrm{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}} \sqrt{\frac{m}{B}}\right) + \mathcal{O}\left(m\log(dT)\log T\right).$

results.notes: Paper's m arms mapped to K; paper's d (resources) declared as d_res. Regret measured as OPT_LP minus expected reward, which upper bounds OPT - REW. Quantum time complexity stated as O~(T).

symbols.delta_gap: LP optimality gap parameter delta = (OPT_LP - max{max_{i in I*} OPT_i, max_{j in J'} OPT_j})/T
symbols.chi: smallest nonzero component of the optimal LP primal solution divided by T
symbols.sigma_min: minimum singular value of the submatrix C_{J*,I*} of the expected consumption matrix

conditions: Assumption 1: LP relaxation has a unique non-degenerate optimal solution
quantum oracle access to rewards and resource consumption
T larger than a problem-dependent constant (used in Lemma 7)
tuning: epsilon_LP <= min{ sigma*chi*log^2 T/(40 min{m^{3/2},d^{3/2}}), 2 b theta min{chi,delta} log^2 T/405, delta/4 }

source.label: thm:quant-bwk2
source.quote: Under \assum{lp}, the expected regret of \algo{quant-bwk2} is upper bounded by $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \left(2+\frac1b\right)\frac{m \sqrt{d} }{b \delta} \log T  + \frac{d^4}{b^2 \min \{\chi^2,\delta^2\} \min\{1,\sigma^2\}} \right)$, with $\epsilon_{\mathrm{LP}} \leq \min \{ \frac{\sigma \chi \log^2T}{40\min\{m^{\frac32},d^{\frac32}\}}, \frac{2b\theta  \min\{\chi,\delta\}\log^2 T}{405}, \frac{\delta}{4} \}$.

results.notes: Combines Proposition 4 (Phase I regret O~((2+1/b) m sqrt(d) log T/(b delta))) and Proposition 5 (Phase II regret O(d^4/(b^2 min{chi^2,delta^2} min{1,sigma^2}))). Phase II analysis also relies on Assumption 2 (warm start), relaxed per Li et al. Paper's delta, sigma renamed to avoid clash with canonical symbols. Algorithm uses the problem-dependent quantities delta, chi, sigma in its tuning.
